system.name: Fernwire
system.description: An invented money transfer app: people send money to bank accounts in other countries, businesses pay many people at once through an API, and a compliance team investigates alerts of possible money laundering.

corpus.included: An invented example, written by hand for the walkthrough page. No code exists; the folders in places are invented.

consumers.name: Sender
consumers.description: A person who sends money from their own bank account to someone's bank account, often in another country.

consumers.name: Business customer
consumers.description: A business, such as a marketplace paying its sellers, that pays many people at once from its own systems.

consumers.name: Compliance analyst
consumers.description: A member of Fernwire's compliance team who reviews alerts of possible money laundering and investigates accounts as cases.

providers.name: Fernwire
providers.description: Fernwire as its users know it: the app and website for sending money, the payouts API, and the compliance team's case console.

parts.name: Mobile app
parts.why: A client that presents Fernwire to senders: part of the mobile app interface.

parts.name: Website
parts.why: A client that presents Fernwire to senders: part of the website interface.

parts.name: Case console app
parts.why: A client that presents alerts, cases and accounts to analysts: part of the case console interface.

parts.name: Payouts API gateway
parts.why: Routes that check a business's API key and pass each request on to Transfers: part of the payouts API interface. The API key only authenticates calls here.

parts.name: Notification sender
parts.why: Delivers the push messages, emails and webhooks that other parts write. It keeps nothing and decides nothing.

components.name: Accounts
components.description: Keeps each person's and business's account, checks identities through the identity verification service, and decides how much each account may send.

parts.name: Account store
parts.why: Storage for accounts. Only Accounts writes to it.

components.name: Transfers
components.description: Takes transfers and payout batches, prices them, and moves the money through the partner bank.

parts.name: Event stream
parts.why: How Transfers delivers the transfer events interface: a stream with no state of its own, and an implementation choice.

components.name: Transfer tracker
components.description: Takes transfers and payout batches and moves each transfer through its statuses, from waiting for money to paid or returned.

components.name: Pricing
components.description: Decides Fernwire's exchange rates and fees from the partner bank's market rates, and sends rate alerts.

components.name: Bank payments
components.description: Sends and receives Fernwire's bank payments through the partner bank, and decides which transfer or batch each incoming payment pays for.

components.name: Risk scoring
components.description: Scores every transfer for signs of money laundering from the account's history, and raises an alert when the score is high.

parts.name: Activity store
parts.why: Where Risk scoring keeps its own record of each account's transfers, with their scores. Only Risk scoring changes it.

parts.name: Scoring rules and model
parts.why: Two ways to score a transfer that give a score in the same form: variants inside Risk scoring, not components of Fernwire.

components.name: Case management
components.description: Keeps the alerts and cases analysts work on, and records each case's decision.

parts.name: Case store
parts.why: Storage for alerts and cases. Only Case management writes to it.

outsideServices.name: Partner bank
outsideServices.description: The bank that holds Fernwire's money, makes and receives bank payments for it, and converts currencies.

outsideServices.name: Identity verification service
outsideServices.description: A service that checks a person's ID document and selfie and says whether they match.

resources.name: Account
resources.description: A person's or a business's account at Fernwire; an account makes many transfers.

resources.name: Transfer
resources.description: Money on its way from one account to one recipient's bank account.

resources.name: Exchange rate
resources.description: Fernwire's price for turning one currency into another, with its fee.

resources.name: Rate alert
resources.description: A sender's request to be told when Fernwire's rate for a currency pair reaches a target.

resources.name: Payout batch
resources.description: A list of payouts a business sends in one go; a batch holds many transfers, and a transfer belongs to at most one batch.

resources.name: Alert
resources.description: A sign of possible money laundering on one account, raised by the risk model.

resources.name: Case
resources.description: An analyst's investigation of one account; a case holds one or more alerts on that account, and an alert belongs to at most one case.

resources.name: Bank payment
resources.description: A payment into or out of one of Fernwire's accounts at the partner bank.

resources.name: Market rate
resources.description: The rate at which the partner bank converts one currency into another for Fernwire.

resources.name: Identity check
resources.description: The identity verification service's check of one person's ID document and selfie.

interfaces.name: website
interfaces.description: Fernwire's website, where senders sign in to send money.

interfaces.name: payouts API
interfaces.description: The HTTP API businesses call from their own systems, with webhooks back to their server.

interfaces.name: case console
interfaces.description: The internal web app where compliance analysts work alerts and cases.

interfaces.name: accounts API
interfaces.description: The contract other components call to use an account's sending limit.

interfaces.name: transfer events
interfaces.description: The stream of events Transfers publishes as each transfer is made and changes status.

interfaces.name: alerts API
interfaces.description: The contract for raising an alert into the analysts' queue.

interfaces.name: identity check API
interfaces.description: The identity verification service's API, which sends each check's outcome back when it is done.

interfaces.name: partner bank API
interfaces.description: The partner bank's API for payments and rates, which sends notices back to Fernwire.

interfaces.name: pricing API
interfaces.description: The contract the Transfer tracker calls for the rate and fee of a transfer.

interfaces.name: bank payments API
interfaces.description: The contract the Transfer tracker calls to pay out transfers and hear about money paid in.

areas.name: Send money
areas.description: Find out what a transfer costs, send it, and follow it until it arrives.

capabilities.name: Get a quote
capabilities.takes: an amount and two currencies
capabilities.gives: what the recipient would get, the fee and the rate

capabilities.name: Send transfer
capabilities.takes: a quote and the recipient's name and bank account, or a past transfer to send again
capabilities.gives: the transfer, with the bank details and reference to pay for it, then a push message or email as it moves and when it arrives

capabilities.name: List transfers
capabilities.takes: nothing
capabilities.gives: the sender's transfers, each with its recipient, amounts and status

areas.name: Set rate alert
areas.description: Be told when the rate is good enough to send.

capabilities.name: Set rate alert
capabilities.takes: a currency pair and a target rate
capabilities.gives: a push message or email when Fernwire's rate reaches the target

areas.name: Open account
areas.description: Become a verified sender with a sending limit.

capabilities.name: Open account
capabilities.takes: the person's name and phone number, a photo of their ID document and a selfie
capabilities.gives: a verified account with its sending limit, or a request for clearer photos

evidence.shows: Invented: the app's screens for quotes, transfers, rate alerts and opening an account.
Invented: the same screens on the website, which sends people to the app to open an account.

areas.name: Pay out
areas.description: Pay many people at once and know when each one is paid.

capabilities.name: Send payout batch
capabilities.takes: a list of payouts, each with a payee's name, bank account and amount
capabilities.gives: the batch, with the total to pay in and its reference, then a webhook to the business's server as each payout is paid or returned

capabilities.name: List payouts
capabilities.takes: a batch
capabilities.gives: each payout in the batch with its status

evidence.shows: Invented: the payouts API routes and the webhook it sends for each payout.

areas.name: Investigate alerts
areas.description: Decide which alerts point to money laundering, and investigate those accounts as cases.

capabilities.name: List alerts
capabilities.takes: a filter, such as open alerts by score
capabilities.gives: alerts, each with its account, the transfers behind it, its score and the model's reason

capabilities.name: Close alert
capabilities.takes: an alert and why it is no concern
capabilities.gives: the alert closed, with the reason on record

capabilities.name: Open case
capabilities.takes: one or more open alerts on one account
capabilities.gives: a case that holds them, assigned to the analyst

capabilities.name: Look up account
capabilities.takes: an account
capabilities.gives: who holds it, how they were verified, their sending limit, and every transfer they made

capabilities.name: Close case
capabilities.takes: a case, its decision, no concern or report to the authorities, and the reasons
capabilities.gives: the case closed, with its decision and reasons on record

evidence.shows: Invented: the alert queue, the case screen and the account page.

areas.name: Use sending limit
areas.description: Count each new transfer against its account's limit.

capabilities.name: Use sending limit
capabilities.takes: an account and an amount
capabilities.gives: the amount counted against the account's limit, or a refusal: not verified, or over the limit

evidence.shows: Invented: the accounts API that Transfers calls before it takes a transfer.

areas.name: Watch transfers
areas.description: Hear about every transfer as it happens.

capabilities.name: Watch transfers
capabilities.takes: a subscription to the transfer events
capabilities.gives: every transfer as it is made and each time its status changes

evidence.shows: Invented: the events Transfers publishes and Risk scoring subscribes to.

areas.name: Raise alert
areas.description: Put a high-scoring account in front of an analyst.

capabilities.name: Raise alert
capabilities.takes: an account, the transfers behind the alert, a score and a reason
capabilities.gives: an open alert in the analysts' queue

evidence.shows: Invented: the alerts API that Risk scoring calls.

areas.name: Check identity
areas.description: Find out whether a person is who their ID document says.

capabilities.name: Check identity
capabilities.takes: a photo of an ID document and a selfie
capabilities.gives: a check in progress, then its outcome, sent back when it is done: passed, or failed with reasons

evidence.shows: Invented: the adapter that sends checks to the identity verification service and receives their outcome.

questions.question: Is the case console its own provider, or part of Fernwire?
questions.answer: Part of Fernwire rather than a provider of its own; analysts see it as Fernwire's compliance tool and it works on Fernwire's own accounts and transfers, but it has its own deployment and consumers, so the rule on separate products does not settle it.

questions.question: Are senders and business customers one consumer?
questions.answer: Two consumers rather than one with a business flag; a business pays many people at once from its own systems and follows batches, goals and resources a sender does not share, though both make transfers from an account.

questions.question: Are the analysts who review alerts and the investigators who work cases one consumer?
questions.answer: One consumer, Compliance analyst, rather than two; both work toward the same goal and in a small team the same person does both, but larger teams split the work, so either reading fits.

questions.question: Is the recipient a resource, or part of a transfer?
questions.answer: Part of Transfer rather than a resource; senders pick a past recipient by sending a transfer again, and no capability works on recipients alone, but a sender would see recipients as things of their own, so either reading fits. A capability such as Edit recipient would make Recipient a resource.

questions.question: Does Risk scoring use Transfers, or does Transfers use Risk scoring?
questions.answer: Risk scoring is the consumer rather than Transfers; Risk scoring wants every transfer, and Transfers neither waits for nor uses the score, though the events flow from Transfers to Risk scoring.

excluded.name: Recipients
excluded.why: People who receive money get it in their own bank account and never use Fernwire, so they are no consumer; their name and bank account are part of each transfer.

excluded.name: Reporting to the authorities
excluded.why: The reporting officer files reports on the authority's own website, outside Fernwire; a case only records the decision to report.

excluded.name: Scoring transfers and raising alerts, seen from the analyst
excluded.why: What Fernwire does on its own, not something the analyst does; the analyst reads the result with List alerts.

excluded.name: Risk model training and threshold tuning
excluded.why: Work on the system, which changes how it scores, rather than with it.

excluded.name: Customer support
excluded.why: Left out to keep the example small; support agents would be a fourth consumer with goals of their own.

excluded.name: Business onboarding, sign-in and account settings
excluded.why: Left out to keep the example small.

excluded.name: Tests, deployment and database migrations
excluded.why: Engineering tooling that builds, checks and ships the system.
